findings.issue: The TestFSMRootsAreDeclared tripwire only matches the quoted component `".metareview"` or `"docs", "metareview"`, so slash-joined literals such as `".metareview/runs.jsonl"` are never checked. That hides one FSM call site that still uses the wrong root. At internal/fsm/cli/wiring.go:139, runsIgnored runs `git check-ignore .metareview/runs.jsonl` in workDir (the work root), and init calls it at run.go:333, but the terminal runs.jsonl row is written under the store root.
findings.consequence: If init runs from a linked worktree, or with a --work-dir other than the main checkout, the WARN_RUNS_NOT_IGNORED check tests ignore status in a checkout that never receives runs.jsonl. If the main checkout does not ignore the file, it can be committed there with no warning, and a spurious warning can appear in the other direction.

findings.issue: TestFSMRootsAreDeclared's doc comment says it covers every line in internal/fsm that builds a .metareview or docs/metareview path, but it misses slash-joined forms. Three sites have no root declaration and pass silently: wiring.go:139 (check-ignore .metareview/runs.jsonl in workDir), run.go:334 (the matching warning text) and record.go:89 (FSMRunDir: ".metareview/runs/" + ...).
findings.consequence: The per-site guard is weaker than it claims. A site written as a single slash-joined literal escapes it, so a store/work confusion can come back unnoticed, which is what #172 set out to prevent. Matching `".metareview/` and `"docs/metareview` prefixes and declaring or fixing the three sites would close it.

findings.issue: The new comment says TestFSMRootsAreDeclared enforces that every .metareview/docs path built in internal/fsm names its root, and docs/ARCHITECTURE.md says every .metareview/docs path names which root it means. That is not true: slash-joined literals are never checked, and at least three such sites have no declaration.
findings.consequence: Readers trust that every root-sensitive path in internal/fsm is declared and checked, while an undeclared slash-form site (runsIgnored checking the work root while the row lives in the store root) stays unchecked.

verdict.reasoning: The tripwire’s predicate only recognizes separate quoted path components, so a literal such as ".metareview/runs.jsonl" bypasses it despite the test claiming to cover every FSM path construction. The diff explicitly classifies runs.jsonl as store-root state, while runsIgnored still accepts workDir unchanged. Therefore the test cannot enforce its stated invariant and does not catch the described store/work-root mismatch.

output.summary: runsIgnored now checks the store root (TestRunsIgnoredChecksTheStoreRoot fails pre-fix: warned about the linked worktree). The tripwire now matches slash-joined literals via buildsRootedPath (TestFSMRootsAreDeclared fails pre-fix on record.go:89) and that site is declared. The comment and ARCHITECTURE.md now describe it as a tripwire, not proof.

findings.issue: The default export destination is still worked out in two places. The CLI rebuilds it itself (the workRoot/storeRoot fallback, then filepath.Join(work, "docs","metareview","fsm", id)) to report `out`, while export.Export builds its own from deps.defaultOutRoot(). Only the comment 'must match export's default' ties them together; export returns no resolved Out and has no DefaultOut helper.
findings.consequence: If someone later changes one default rule (the fallback, the path layout, or the root choice) and not the other, the CLI will report an `out` that differs from where the bundle was actually written, with no compile-time signal.

findings.issue: AC-1.5 in #172 asks for the two roots to be described in both §4 (The FSM) and §6 (State, evidence & storage). The diff adds the description only to §6 and a §10 gotcha; §4 still says nothing about roots or worktrees.
findings.consequence: One stated acceptance criterion is only partly met. Someone reading §4 to learn how FSM runs and exports are laid out will not find the store/work split there.
